opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is full-time Analyst. Requested write to Payroll; full-time employees can have up to write (admin only if role owns the system). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E026 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting employee information. The HR note lists Alyssa as full-time Analyst, which would allow write to Payroll (Analyst does not own Payroll, so admin is not allowed). However, the Security note states the Security DB shows E026 is a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read (write requires advanced training for contractors). Given conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive, security-verified facts: contractor with basic training => maximum read. Since requested write exceeds the maximum, grant read.
